planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring after frost in deep, well-drained, alkaline soil; Ohadi is a female cultivar and needs a compatible male pollinator blooming at the same time.

directions: Ohadi is one of Iran's five major commercial pistachio cultivars, grown extensively in the Kerman and Rafsanjan districts alongside Akbari, Fandoghi, and Kaleh Ghouchi. Its nuts are medium-sized with a notably high kernel oil content, a trait that makes the variety popular for roasting and traditional Iranian confections. Like other pistachio cultivars, Ohadi needs a long, hot, arid summer and substantial winter chill to properly fill and split its shell, and it performs poorly in humid climates. Plant in deep, well-drained, alkaline soil with a compatible male pollinator nearby, and harvest in early autumn once hulls loosen and nuts show their natural shell split.
sources: Fatty Acids-Based Quality Index to Differentiate Worldwide Commercial Pistachio Cultivars (PMC)
University of California Cooperative Extension — Pistachio Production Manual

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring after frost in deep, well-drained, alkaline soil; Ahmad Aghaei is a female cultivar and needs a compatible male pollinator blooming at the same time.

directions: Ahmad Aghaei is a well-known Iranian pistachio cultivar prized for an unusually large, long nut, ranking among the biggest-nutted cultivars commercially grown in Iran's Kerman region. It flowers in mid-season, placing its bloom window between the earlier Kaleh Ghouchi and later Akbari, a detail growers must account for when siting pollinator trees nearby. As with other Pistacia vera selections, it demands a hot, dry, low-humidity summer and significant winter chill to fill and split its shell reliably, and struggles in humid climates. Grow in deep, well-drained, alkaline soil and expect a long juvenile period before the tree reaches full bearing.
sources: Fatty Acids-Based Quality Index to Differentiate Worldwide Commercial Pistachio Cultivars (PMC)
Assessment of phenolic profile and antioxidant power of five pistachio cultivars from Iran (PMC)

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring after frost in deep, well-drained soil; Napoletana is a female cultivar and needs a compatible male pollinator blooming at the same time.

directions: Napoletana is one of the three traditional local varieties recognized within Sicily's Pistacchio Verde di Bronte DOP, grown on the volcanic slopes of Mount Etna alongside Cerasuola and Bianca. It is valued for its vivid green kernel color and intense flavor, qualities that drive the strong reputation and premium pricing of Bronte-grown pistachios. Like other Pistacia vera selections, it needs a hot, dry summer and enough winter chill to fill and split its shell, but it has adapted over centuries to the mineral-rich volcanic soils and Mediterranean climate of the Etna foothills. Plant in deep, well-drained soil with a compatible male pollinator nearby, and expect the pronounced biennial bearing habit typical of the species.
sources: Pistacchio Verde di Bronte DOP Consortium product specification
Slow Food Foundation for Biodiversity — Presidia

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring after frost in deep, well-drained soil; Cerasuola is a female cultivar and needs a compatible male pollinator blooming at the same time.

directions: Cerasuola is a traditional Sicilian pistachio variety grown within the Pistacchio Verde di Bronte DOP on the volcanic slopes of Mount Etna, named for the deep cherry-red hue of its hull. Alongside Napoletana and Bianca, it forms part of the historic local gene pool that growers have maintained for generations on Etna's terraced orchards. It shares the species' demanding need for a hot, dry summer and adequate winter chill, but has become particularly well adapted to the free-draining, mineral-rich volcanic soil of its native growing area. Harvest in early autumn as hulls loosen, and plant with a compatible male pollinator since pistachio is wind-pollinated and dioecious.
sources: Pistacchio Verde di Bronte DOP Consortium product specification
Slow Food Foundation for Biodiversity — Presidia

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring after frost in deep, well-drained soil; Bianca is a female cultivar and needs a compatible male pollinator blooming at the same time.

directions: Bianca is the third of the traditional local varieties recognized within Sicily's Pistacchio Verde di Bronte DOP, grown alongside Napoletana and Cerasuola on the volcanic slopes of Mount Etna. Its name refers to a paler hull color relative to its two orchard companions, though like them it yields the vivid green kernel prized in Bronte-grown pistachios. It requires the same hot, dry summer and winter chill as other Pistacia vera selections, and has adapted over a long cultivation history to Etna's rocky, mineral-rich volcanic terraces. Plant in deep, well-drained soil with a compatible male pollinator nearby, and expect the pronounced biennial bearing typical of the species.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring after frost in deep, well-drained, alkaline soil; Siirt is a female cultivar and needs a compatible male pollinator blooming at the same time.

directions: Siirt is one of Turkey's leading commercial pistachio cultivars, widely planted in the Gaziantep and southeastern Anatolia region that produces the bulk of the country's crop. It is valued for a large, well-filled nut and a shell that splits cleanly, traits that have made it a preferred choice for Turkish growers over older local landraces. As with other Pistacia vera cultivars, it needs a hot, arid summer and substantial winter chill to develop properly, and underperforms in humid climates outside its native growing range. Plant grafted trees in deep, well-drained, alkaline soil with a compatible male pollinator nearby, and harvest in early autumn as hulls loosen and shells show their natural split.
sources: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) — pistachio production country profiles
Turkish Journal of Agriculture and Forestry
